Use on recurring task-d6325d6f grids: repeated framed square/rectangular tiles on a 0 background, with solid-color interior patches and uniform border color (demos used border 2/3/4, patch colors varied). Tile pitch leaves narrow blank gutters (usually 1–2 cells).

## Rule
1. Detect the repeated tile lattice (do not assume a fixed pitch or tile size). Each tile has a border and a solid-color interior patch.
2. Preserve every original tile cell and all background not involved in a bridge.
3. For each tile row, inspect the interior-patch colors across its tiles. Whenever the same patch color appears at two or more columns, color the blank horizontal gutter(s) between those matching positions with that color. Bridge through intervening tile positions by filling only the gutters, never overwrite their framed tiles or interiors.
4. Apply the analogous rule vertically: in each tile column, repeated patch colors bridge the blank gutter band(s) between their tile rows, filling only the gutter cells aligned with the patch interior.
5. Keep colors independent; do not connect across different tile rows/columns or infer a diagonal connection. Preserve the outer background, borders, and unmatched gaps.

## Evidence / pitfalls
Two demos confirmed this on different tile sizes, lattice pitches, palettes, and layouts. In one, repeated color-3 and color-1/other marker patches were connected in the gutters both horizontally and vertically. In another, color-8 and color-4 patch groups were bridged across gutters while intervening tile bodies stayed unchanged. A first speculative attempt that drew long center-to-center lines was incorrect: only the intervening blank gutter cells are recolored, not the tile bodies. Re-derive the lattice and patch colors for each fresh instance; dimensions and palette vary.",
